title: Minimax Risk in Randomized Trials with Missing-at-Random Outcomes and Shrinking Arrival Probability
banked_reason: The proposal all-(n,d,q) q-uniform, dimension-sensitive frontier is not delivered: the middle full-record converse remains open; delivered tier incremental, below the field floor.
gap_reasons: The proposal's all-(n,d,q) q-uniform, dimension-sensitive frontier is not delivered: this node remains open, and the proved below-elbow/parametric slices do not settle the stated shrinking-arrival stress path.
The framing accurately discloses these limitations, but the delivered package is therefore a companion-level collection of boundary results rather than the field-level frontier posed by the project.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved a complete-case estimator bound, a parametric lower bound, near-complete and low-effective-arrival matched regions, and a fixed-overlap lower transfer. It could not construct the exactly normalized full-record middle-range prior pair or a log-improved estimator, so the advertised shrinking-arrival stress path remains unmatched. A future retry needs genuinely new q-uniform witness and estimation machinery rather than another solve of the same frozen graph.
tldr: A balanced randomized trial reveals \(X,A,S\) for every enrollee, while the binary fixed-horizon outcome arrives under cell-specific MAR with certified floor \(q\). The note proves the universal lower bound \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,q}\geq256^{-1}\min\{1,(nq)^{-1}\}\) and explicit zero-filled and complete-case mixed-count upper bounds. For every fixed finite \(K_{\mathrm{eff}}\), these certificates match whenever \(d\leq K_{\mathrm{eff}}\sqrt{nq}\), and the corresponding honest connected-interval length is matched; if \(nq\leq1\), constant risk and length hold for every \(d\). A recordwise garbling of Zeng et al., strengthened by alphabet nesting, proves for fixed \(q_0\in(0,1/2)\) and all \(q\leq q_0\) the all-alphabet bound \(\mathfrak R_{n,d,q}\gtrsim_{q_0}\min\{1,n^{-1}+[d/\{n\log(en)\}]^2\}\). A generic midpoint conversion now gives \(\mathfrak L_{n,d,q,\alpha}\geq2(\mathfrak R_{n,d,q}-4\alpha)_+\); hence \(d\geq n\log(en)\) has constant honest length when \(\alpha\leq c_Z(q_0)/8\). This is a sufficiently-high-confidence fixed-overlap corollary, not an arbitrary-\(\alpha\) converse. The \(q\)-uniform dimension-sensitive frontier between the effective-arrival elbow and saturation remains open.
gap: The catalogued rare-arrival lower certificate stops when \(q\log^2(e+nq)\) exceeds its universal boundary, and the catalogued near-complete lower certificate begins only at \(q\ge1/2\). Existing all-\(q\) upper certificates do not supply a uniform converse on the intervening parameter-law class.
fill: The project tests the explicit piecewise \(\mathfrak r_{n,d,q}\) by building the missing paired full-record priors with a fixed-constant point-risk specialization and, for every fixed \(\alpha<1/2\), confidence-specific \(\beta,\delta\) satisfying \(2\alpha+2\beta+\delta<1\). The exact two-mixture reduction converts their calibrated total variation, ATE separation, and concentration into expected connected-interval length. The estimator selector, rare and near-complete lower slices, and complete-arrival reduction are inherited infrastructure rather than novelty claims.
